([[Branson, Missouri]]) | college = [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 6 | draft_team = [[Washington Wizards]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Washington Wizards]] | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] (2025) * Second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2025) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2024 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2024]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2024) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2024) * [[Texas Mr. Basketball]] (2023) }} '''Richard Earl''' "'''Tre'''" '''Johnson III''' (born March 7, 2006) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] and was the 2025 [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]]. Johnson was selected sixth overall by the Wizards in the [[2025 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Johnson grew up in [[Dallas|Dallas, Texas]] and attended [[Lake Highlands High School]].{{cite web |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/big-names-eye-lake-highlands-basketball-star-tre-johnson-2024s-no-1-prospect/ |title=Big names eye Lake Highlands basketball star Tre Johnson, 2024's no. 1 prospect |first=Jett |last=Beachum |website=[[CBS Texas]] |date=February 19, 2023 |access-date=May 24, 2023}} He averaged 23.8 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game as a sophomore.{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/sep/25/nations-top-junior-recruit-considering-ua-visit/|title=Nation's top junior recruit considering UA visit|first=Richard|last=Davenport|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=September 25, 2022|access-date=May 24, 2023}} During his junior year, Johnson and Lake Highlands took part in the City of Palms Tournament, where he averaged 23 points per game.{{cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=May 17, 2023 |title=Tre Johnson includes KU basketball on list of 6: recruiting |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article275446476.html |access-date=May 24, 2023 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]]}} At the end of the season, he led Wildcats to their first state championship since 1968 and scored 29 points in the team's 55–44 win in the state championship game against [[Beaumont United High School]].{{cite web |last=McFarland |first=Shawn |date=March 12, 2023 |title=Tre Johnson, top recruit of 2024, takes over 6A state title game |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2023/03/11/tre-johnson-takeover-nations-top-2024-recruit-leads-lake-highlands-to-6a-state-title/ |access-date=May 24, 2023 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}} Johnson finished the season averaging 21.8 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game and was named [[Texas Mr. Basketball]].{{cite web |date=March 14, 2023 |title=BREAKING: Lake Highlands G Tre Johnson and Holliday F Jalynn Bristow named Mr. and Miss Texas Basketball Players of the Year |url=https://www.texasbasketball.com/article/2023/03/19/breaking-lake-highlands-g-tre-johnson-and-holliday-f-jalynn-bristow-named-mr-and-miss-texas-basketball-players-of-the-year |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=[[Dave Campbell's Texas Football#Dave Campbell's Texas Basketball|Dave Campbell's Texas Basketball]]}} After the end of the school year, he transferred to [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]] in [[Branson, Missouri]].{{cite web |last=Wheeler |first=Wyatt D. |date=June 16, 2023 |title=Tre Johnson, 2024 basketball star, to attend Link Academy in Branson |url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/high-school/2023/06/16/tre-johnson-2024-basketball-star-to-attend-link-academy-in-branson/70332341007/ |access-date=June 20, 2023 |work=[[Springfield News-Leader]]}} Johnson produced 15.5 points, 3.6 assists and 3.3 rebounds per contest while shooting nearly 40% from 3-point range and 90.5% from the free throw line during his senior year. Johnson led the Lions to a 26–7 record. Johnson was selected to play in the [[2024 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Myah |date=January 23, 2024 |title=Tre Johnson, Liam McNeeley make 2024 McDonald's All American game |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2024/01/23/texas-signee-tre-johnson-liam-mcneeley-make-2024-mcdonalds-all-american-game-rosters/ |access-date=January 26, 2024 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}} ===Recruiting=== Johnson was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web |last=McFarland |first=Shawn |date=July 20, 2022 |title=Lake Highlands five-star Tre Johnson is catching everyone's attention — even LeBron James |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2022/07/20/lake-highlands-five-star-tre-johnson-is-catching-everyones-attention-even-lebron-james/ |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}} He was ranked the top overall recruit by [[247Sports]], [[ESPN]], [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and [[On3.com|On3]] throughout his junior year until he was surpassed by [[Dylan Harper]] during the summer of 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article271680497.html|title=Kentucky focusing recruiting efforts on nation's No. 1 junior. He's visiting this weekend.|first=Cameron|last=Drummond|work=[[Lexington Herald Leader]]|date=January 27, 2023|access-date=May 24, 2023}}{{cite web |last=Drummond |first=Cameron |date=September 15, 2022 |title=A prized UK prospect is the top player in the 2024 class —and other recruiting links. |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article265656776.html |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=[[Lexington Herald Leader]]}}{{cite web|url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/no-1-prospect-tre-johnson-expanding-his-game-as-coaches-swarm|title=No. 1 prospect Tre Johnson expanding his game as coaches swarm|first=Jason|last=Jordan|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 24, 2023|access-date=May 26, 2023}} On November 15, 2023, Johnson committed to playing college basketball for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] after considering an offer from [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]].{{cite web |last=Bass |first=Tobias |date=November 15, 2023 |title=Texas lands 5-star guard Tre Johnson: What's next for the Longhorns? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5066739/2023/11/15/texas-basketball-recruiting-tre-johnson/ |access-date=November 15, 2023 |website=[[The Athletic]]}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2024}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Tre Johnson | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Dallas|Dallas, TX]] | highschool = [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]] (MO) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 184 | 40 = | commitdate = November 15, 2023 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | On3 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 95 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2024 | rivals ref title = Texas 2024 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2024 Texas Longhorns Recruiting Class | rivals school = Texas | scout s = | espn schoolid = 251 | rivals overall = 5 | 247 overall = 6 | On3 overall = 7 | espn overall = 5 | accessdate = December 24, 2023 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Tre Johnson.jpg|thumb|Johnson with the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] in 2025]] At the beginning of the season, Johnson was named to the [[Jerry West Award]] watch list and [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] watch list. In his debut game against [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], Johnson had 29 points, five rebounds, four assists, two steals, and one block. On February 26, 2025, Johnson broke [[Kevin Durant]]'s freshman single-game program record by scoring 39 points in an overtime loss to [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]].{{cite web |date=February 26, 2025 |title=Arkansas tops Texas in OT despite Johnson's 39 that breaks Durant's freshman Texas single-game mark |url=https://apnews.com/article/texas-arkansas-tre-johnson-basketball-4efe4b50235d42938a2a70705194d403 |access-date=March 13, 2025 |website=[[Associated Press]]}} In a win that pushed Texas into the last four in of the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] according to many bracketologists, Johnson scored a game-high 20 points and hit the go-ahead 3-pointer in double overtime against the No. 14 [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] in the second round of the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/texas-texas-am-score-79057acb4f435b4f930961fe8a757f9d|title=Tre Johnson's 3 in double OT puts Texas ahead to stay in win over No. 14 Texas A&M at SEC Tourney|first=Teresa|last=Walker|website=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 13, 2025|access-date=March 13, 2025}}{{cite web |last=Lunardi |first=Joe |date=March 13, 2025 |title=Men's Bracketology: 2025 NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/page/bracketology/ncaa-bracketology-2025-march-madness-men-field-predictions |access-date=March 13, 2025 |website=[[ESPN]]}} Johnson ended the season averaging 19.9 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, shooting 39.7% from the three. He was named [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]].{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Lowe: Projected lottery pick Tre Johnson performing well in draft workouts |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rookie/2025/06/20/texas-tre-johnson-nba-draft-workouts-rumors/84294632007/ |access-date=December 17, 2025 |work=Rookie Wire |date=June 20, 2025}} ==Professional career== Johnson was selected with the sixth overall pick by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-draft-order|title=2025 NBA Draft Results: Picks 1-59|website=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2025|access-date=June 26, 2025}} He made his professional debut on October 23, 2025 in a game against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], coming off the bench to register 16 points, including 4-of-8 shooting from three-point range. It was the franchise's highest scoring debut by a rookie since 1992.{{cite web|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rookie/2025/10/23/wizards-tre-johnson-nba-debut-stats/86858829007/|title=Tre Johnson had the best scoring debut by a Wizards rookie since 1992|first=Cody|last=Taylor|website=therookiewire.usatoday.com|date=October 23, 2025|access-date=October 24, 2025}} ==National team career== Johnson played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States team]] in the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], averaging 11.1 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 2.6 assists in seven games to place fourth in the tournament.{{cite web |last=McFarland |first=Shawn |date=June 16, 2023 |title=Lake Highlands' Tre Johnson named to 2023 Team USA U19 national team |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2023/06/16/lake-highlands-five-star-guard-tre-johnson-named-to-2023-team-usa-u19-national-team/ |access-date=June 21, 2023 |work=[[The ==Personal life== Johnson's father, Richard Johnson Jr., played college basketball at [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] before transferring to [[Midwestern State Mustangs|Midwestern State]].{{cite web |last=McFarland |first=Shawn |date=January 20, 2022 |title=At Lake Highlands, one of the nation's best sophomore basketball players is turning heads |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2022/01/20/at-lake-highlands-one-of-the-nations-best-sophomore-basketball-players-is-turning-heads/ |access-date=May 24, 2023 |work=[[The web|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/12/17/tre-johnson-cementing-his-place-at-the-top-of-recruiting-polls/69733889007/|title=Tre Johnson cementing his place at the top of recruiting polls|first=Nick|last=Wilson|work=[[The News-Press]]|date=December 17, 2022|access-date=May 24, 2023}} He has two younger brothers, Royce Johnson and Jamari Riley.
